text:
alex: FYI observed a p95/p99 spike for model-redwood-open-7b-v3 after today's tokenizer cutover. Customer reports API timeouts and ~2-3x p99 on long-context jobs (~8k tokens).

maria: ugh. are these coming from Hosted or Dedicated? any particular region?

alex: predominantly hosted-us-west. A few dedicated customers also saw regressed tails. It started ~09:05 UTC when tokenizer v2 rolled.

jordan: can we confirm whether kv-cache hits dropped? My hypothesis: token boundary change -> cache misses -> more KV loads -> higher latency.

maria: good point. I pulled logs. prefix_kv_hit_rate for the model dropped from ~0.82 to 0.41 around the same time. attaching a snippet.

alex: (paste)
```
2026-03-15T09:04:58Z model=redwood-open-7b-v3 prefix_kv_hit=0.81
2026-03-15T09:05:12Z model=redwood-open-7b-v3 prefix_kv_hit=0.40
2026-03-15T09:06:00Z model=redwood-open-7b-v3 p95_ms=227 p99_ms=842
```

sasha: OK that matches kv miss theory. Any tokenization diffs that would break existing cached prefixes?

maria: tokenizer v2 changes BPE merge ranks for some byte sequences — small deltas normally, but for long user prompts that reuse prefixes the token boundaries shifted. So previously cached prefix tokens no longer matched and the runtime was forced to re-encode and re-populate caches on every request.

liam: is this a server-side config bug or an expected regression from the new tokenizer? We need mitigation ASAP (canary rollback?).

alex: ops-bot, open incident please and start a canary rollback to tokenizer v1 for the affected model in us-west.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260315-001 opened by alex. Initiating canary rollback to tokenizer v1 on 10% of us-west capacity. Will report progress. :rotating_light:

jordan: while rollback is running, we should also create a quick shim that normalizes tokenization for cached prefixes: re-tokenize incoming prompts with tokenizer-v1 for cache-key calculation only. That would avoid full cutover while rollout completes.

maria: we can add a cache-key compatibility mode in the router: when model==redwood-open-7b-v3 and tokenization_cutover==true fallback to tokenizer-v1 cache-key generation. Easy small change in routing layer.

alex: sounds good. estimate time?

maria: I can patch the router in ~30m, release with a 5-minute canary, then ramp. Risk low since it's just cache key hashing.

liam: while that's happening, let's capture repro steps so support can triage customers: 1) use model redwood-open-7b-v3 2) send request with ~6k-9k token prompt that repeats a common prefix 3) observe p99 >> baseline 4) check prefix_kv_hit_rate metric.

alex: adding to support playbook and notifying impacted tenants. Also adding an eval set to run locally to compare tokenizer-v1 vs v2 tokenizations for sample customer prompts.

sasha: quick note: some customers saw API 504s (gateway timeout) due to downstream increase in per-request CPU while re-populating caches. We should increase request timeouts temporarily from 30s -> 60s for hosted endpoints for this model to reduce client-side errors during rollback. Thoughts?

maria: agree. Increasing request timeout to 60s for the model-route in hosted is safe short-term. Rolling that in now.

ops-bot: Canary rollback to tokenizer v1 at 10% completed. Observed p95 improvement from 220ms -> 130ms on canary nodes. Planning ramp to 50% in 10m.

jordan: once router compatibility mode is live we can fully revert to tokenizer v2 without user impact. But we'll need to run long-run regression tests: run 24h KV-cache stability job and synthetic 8k-token traces.

alex: agreed. Priority list: (1) router cache-key shim (maria) (2) ramp rollback to 50/100% as needed (ops) (3) timeout bump (maria) (done) (4) long-run tests and tokenization diff report (jordan + alex) (5) postmortem and checklist for future tokenizer onboards.

liam: also flag billing implications: cost per token may spike due to re-encodes. finance notified.

maria: deployed router shim (canary) — logs show prefix_kv_hit_rate on shim nodes rose back to ~0.79 and p99 dropped ~55%. Rolling to 100% router traffic for the model.

ops-bot: Rollback ramp to 50% complete. p95 on 50% nodes ~130ms. No new 504s observed after timeout bump.

alex: great work. I'll draft a short status update for customers and mark the incident as mitigation-in-progress. After long-run tests pass we'll flip tokenizer v2 and keep router compatibility for 48h before full removal.

sasha: postmortem notes request: include root cause (tokenizer boundary changes affecting cache keys), detection (metric drop in prefix_kv_hit_rate + p99 spike), mitigations (rollback, router shim, timeout bump), and long-term fix (either stable tokenization contract or hashed-normalized prefix scheme).

maria: logging note for SRE: add metric 'tokenization_variant' tag to request traces so future cutovers can be segmented quickly.

alex: thanks all. will follow up with timeline and customer comms. (reacted with :thumbsup:)
